holisticNarrative.summary:
The OneConnect evidence set is unusual because it pairs a very thin b(10) disclosure with a much richer SMART-on-FHIR implementation guide. The one-page EHI export document says the package is a ZIP containing encounter C-CDAs and that additional chart attachments are planned later. That wording is a direct signal that the documented package path is not fully mature as a complete patient-record export surface.

At the same time, the FHIR guide provides substantial technical detail across major clinical domains and includes concrete payload examples. For migration engineers, this means there is a viable extraction path for core clinical content, but model reconstruction still requires substantial inference: there is no machine-readable schema, no explicit relationship map, and no complete account of designated-record-set administrative domains such as billing, claims, or payments.

Practically, this is not a zero-capability product. It is a standards-projection-heavy export posture where clinical portability is plausible but full-fidelity migration confidence remains constrained by documentation gaps and likely projection loss outside the US Core-focused surface.
standoutObservations: Risky: b(10) PDF explicitly says the ZIP contains C-CDAs "for now" and attachments will be added later.
Impressive: API guide covers broad clinical domains with concrete examples and US Core profile references.
Unclear: no machine-readable schema or explicit PK/FK/constraint documentation accompanies either export path.
Important scope point: missing audit logs were not treated as EHI gaps because audit logs are outside designated-record-set EHI scope.

notableFacts: Both primary export artifacts identify the product as "OneConnect Version 0".
The certified EHI export document is a single page and describes a ZIP that contains encounter-level C-CDA files.
The EHI export document explicitly says additional chart attachments (e.g., PDF/images) will be added later.
The FHIR API guide explicitly supports a backend multi-patient SMART app model for exporting clinical data for groups of patients.

FHIR examples cover major clinical domains (Patient, AllergyIntolerance, CarePlan, CareTeam, Condition, Device, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference, Observation, Goal, Immunization, MedicationRequest, Procedure, Provenance).
No machine-readable schema artifact (OpenAPI/JSON schema/XSD/DDL) is present in the collected OneConnect files.
